The Game PK: an unofficial PC-88VA / PC-88VA2 port of an arcade game
(MS-DOS 4.0 disk)

This is an independent, unofficial program. It is not made, endorsed or
supported by the owners of the original game or by NEC.

This disk holds MS-DOS 4.0 for the PC-88VA (FreeDOS-88VA project, MIT
licence, see LICENSE.TXT and README.TXT) and PK.COM (two-clause BSD
licence, see PKLICENS.TXT). It contains no data from the arcade game: you
need your own copies of its ROM files.

ROM files
---------
PK needs eight files, recognised by size and CRC-32 (any names): the four
program ROMs of either version A or version B, and four shared ROMs.

    size   CRC-32 (A)  CRC-32 (B)
    4096   FEE263B3    C1E6AB10     program 1
    4096   39D1FC83    1A6FB2D4     program 2
    4096   02083B03    BCDD1BEB     program 3
    4096   7A36FE55    817D94E3     program 4

    size   CRC-32
    4096   0C944964     tiles
    4096   958FEDF9     sprites
      32   2FC650BD     colours
     256   3EB3A8E4     colour lookup

Copy them to the root of this disk under MS-DOS, or on a PC run

    python3 install_roms.py pk-msdos4.d88 ROMS.zip

(the zip, or a directory, holding the files) which writes
pk-msdos4-roms.d88; install_roms.py needs pcengine_disk.py beside it.
Version B is what game-extraction-toolbox
(https://github.com/shawngmc/game-extraction-toolbox) extracts from the
game's Steam re-release; its zip can be given to install_roms.py as it is.
PK names the first file it does not find. PK DIRECTORY looks for them in
another directory.

Optional host-fitted FM (FM-capable builds only)
----------------------------------------------
The experimental FM build can load private FMVOICE.DAT voices. The released
v0.1 SSG-only PK.COM cannot do this. Use an FM-capable base disk and run:

    python3 -m pip install numpy
    python3 -I install_roms.py pk-msdos4.d88 Release_3.dll output.d88 --fit-fm

Keep fmfit.py, fmdata.py and pcengine_disk.py beside install_roms.py.
SOURCE must also include the 256-byte waveform PROM, CRC-32 A9CC86BF.
Fitting runs on the host PC, not the VA. The output holds ROMs and derived
voices: do not distribute it. The source disk is not modified, and existing
output paths are refused. The supported Steam Release_3.dll is verified
and extracted directly (no external extractor required). Other DLL versions
are rejected. Extracted ROM directories and zip files also remain accepted.

FM builds use validated fitted voices at startup. If unavailable, a verified
waveform PROM allows quick harmonic generation; otherwise SSG is used.
PK /S forces SSG. PK /F regenerates quick voices (not host precision) and
can overwrite a fitted cache: do not use /F to play host-fitted voices.
F10 can switch between FM and SSG when FM voices are available.

Running
-------
The disk starts PK from AUTOEXEC.BAT. The game needs a monitor that
accepts 15 kHz (320x224 at 15.98 kHz, 59.9 Hz), and the machine must be
started in 15 kHz mode (CRT mode: DIP switch SW1 off); started at 24 kHz,
PK stops with a message. It also needs memory up to segment 6080h (about
390 KB); builds with the expanded SGP sprite cache require segment 6700h
(412 KB). The loader checks the DOS allocation before using this memory.
Picture the game with the monitor turned clockwise: the top of the
game is on the left of the screen. Standard builds use YM2203 SSG sound;
FM-capable builds can use fitted FM voices as described above.

First an alignment screen is shown for about 5 seconds: let the monitor
adjust itself, move the picture with keypad 8 2 4 6 (or the cursor keys),
start at once with RETURN or SPACE.

Keys (in the game's orientation):

    keypad 8 2 4 6, cursor keys   move
    5                             coin
    1, 2                          1 player, 2 player start
    F10                           DIP switches, sound test
    ESC                           restart the machine

F10 also offers DRAW: 60 FPS (default) or 30 FPS. Select DRAW with up/down
and change it with left/right. Only graphics are halved at 30 FPS; input,
audio and original-game interrupts still run every vertical interrupt.
Menu/sound-test operation is not halved. The setting lasts until reboot and
is not saved to disk. These are target draw rates, not measured frame rates:
if native work overruns a frame, either setting can still slow the game.

DIP switch changes restart the game; they are not saved.
